comments.value:
I believe the system has needed an overhaul for a while now. There needs to be more information given to players on what the status is of an invite, a chat system of some sort to send messages like "Hey sorry, busy," and over all there should be feedback in instances where the player is not the host of the world. 

Bagel spoke briefly on jaded players, and honestly I've seen this first hand many times. Not being accepted and having no idea what's going on when you cast invite requests pushes some people's state of mind to bad places and they assume the worst case scenario, ultimately leaving the game for long period of times or turning bitter towards others who have established groups to join. 

That's where hopefully more information might help keep people connected. The status update where you can display a short message and your availability was a huge step in the right direction, but it needs to go farther than that. People need to be able to see if the invite requests are timed out, not accepted, and people should get a message if they aren't the worlds host like friends only or invite worlds.

This in the end won't fix everything, but at least having more information in game will help direct people to what's going on instead of standing in a world wondering what will happen.

There's a number of things that are leading to the game's steady decline. I'd say the biggest one is the lack of a "game" all vrchat is, is a social vr experience where the social aspect barely functions. I agree fixing the atrocity that is just sending someone an invite request would improve things dramatically but there are much more pressing things vrchat requires if it wants to maintain or even grow again. (like actual world scripting) (also lets not forget that it wasn't that long ago where people were totally unable to request invites from their friends at all)

As much as this would help, I don't think they'll implement it anytime soon. It's not just lack of community cohesion, it's also poor developer decisions.

Lots of people are trying to find other places to go because of things like the unfair avatar rating system, or because of class warfare based on user titles.
I've seen many streamers end up quitting either because of lack of viewers, or because of the constant wild and rampant crashing of either the game or someone using a crashing shader.

Fixing this would only be a small bandage in comparison to the gushing holes put in by the devs to "fix" other things.

You want an example of the devs -not- listening to community feedback? Look at the response by Tupper over at this request: https://vrchat.canny.io/feature-requests/p/adjust-volume-of-individuals

"We believe adjusting the volume of individuals isn't the best approach. We're looking into alternate spatialization systems (or adjusting the one we're already using) that should help solve this problem in an automatic and natural way."

Absolutely NO ONE wanted an automated system, but they're gonna do it anyway.

865 people wanted a simple volume slider for individuals, but they're gonna automate it because the devs know what's best for the players somehow.

If someone manages to make a game that's better than Vrchat, I'll definitely switch to it. All they gotta do is listen to their player base more than the devs do here.

This is really important, but knowing the current stance of the developers and how they think they know best (sometimes), I don't think I'll see this implemented any time soon. I've been told a number of times and experienced the lack of community cohesion, and there has been lots of trolls crashing worlds. That's the whole reason I essentially quit playing until a big change for the better happens in favor of what the PLAYERS want.

Meanwhile public players are left out of the picture. We're stuck dealing with the RNG of finding other individuals who can hold a normal conversation. While also dealing with the Trust and Rank System that in some cases makes it impossible for mutes to communicate anymore and makes it almost impossible for new users to meet people. It's no wonder that the numbers are going down as the community is pushing everyone into the bubbles of influencer communities which are highly toxic and filled with people that despise outsiders. Hell, there's no longer events going on either.

Public players have the right to find a way to have discussions and talking to other individuals without issues. We demand a group finder system where we can create our own groups with names (Topics) and descriptions and a browser for said groups so we can find people to talk to. We want to escape the current status quo of being stuck in public without any chance of escape without spending money on influencers.

Some of us want to take the first step, the invite and request system isn't part of that first step and currently for public players we are being mistreated with a horrible Trust and Rank System (REMOVE NAMEPLATE COLORS AND REDUCE IT TO A TRUST SYSTEM WITH SLIDERS FOR NO RANKS), influencers calling all of us trash and vermin + worse, completely unmoderated environment where we players need to do the moderation action instead of a voluntary moderation corps, complete RNG at finding decent individiuals you can conversate with meaning you can spend hours upon hours trying to find individuals just to talk about ONE specific thing, staff has directed all events to be community driven and therefore events are no longer being hosted for public users and everything event wise is influencer community driven meaning exclusivity is a common practice.

If they don't want to clean up Public, give us a group finder. We don't want to be cogs in the machines of the influencers who requires money from lonely and psychologically vulnerable individuals to continue making their VRChat content and to foster their communities. 

Please don't neglect us anymore.
@{5ad28c0c839dc146dd2b6d56|full_name}: Make this a canny request. I think there needs to be more moderation in publics. I miss publics so much.

@{5c590f0a028b3c4b40ee6c2c|full_name}: Make this a canny. They told us to use this to voice our concerns so we will flood it. I agree that my suggestion is only a patch but I need people like you to throw new solutions and ideas out there. I am not the fix all. Never will be. We all are the fix all. If nothing less than showing future devs what not to do when making social VR games.
@{5ae711a086105b13a3fc87fc|full_name}: I'm not doing that, I have given up all hope.
@{5ad28c0c839dc146dd2b6d56|full_name}: I've also given up. i still don't know why i bother to read posts here.

If there were maybe a sort of invite plus where each individual already in the room could invite others - not auto-join like friends plus, and that each new person would be labelled by the person who invited them, I believe that it could resolve a lot of this. Those who became undesirable,  would be known by all, and others could still privately talk to the one who did the invite privately about the individual to prevent future issues.
@{5c590f0a028b3c4b40ee6c2c|full_name}: I agree, I think the "devs know best" mentality that they have is really hurting the game.
@{5ad28c0c839dc146dd2b6d56|full_name}: Why would you need a "Group Finder" system? This isn't an MMO, you're not searching for a party to raid a dungeon with.
@{5ae711a086105b13a3fc87fc|full_name}: Good idea. I've put together a post here: https://vrchat.canny.io/feature-requests/p/listening-better-about-what-the-community-wants

I believe that “9k to 5k” is a bit of an exaggerated and jaded stat. The game according to steam charts has had around a 5.5k players on average and the next spiked up to 7.1k January 2019, and now it’s just going back to it’s normal amount of average players, plus we now have the people that stopped playing through steam all together and switched to oculus, and the new players that play on oculus quest. So we are probably more accurately sitting at 6-7k players probably on average.

I’m not saying the problem you’ve pointed out isn’t a problem, what I’m saying it isn’t a problem that causes players to just stop playing because of a quality of life fix. Do I want this part of the game to bug fixed? Yes. Do I think the game is dying like everyone else and their mother? No. We have the same amount of player base when started, actually we have more than what we started with if we exclude the boom of Jan 2018. The boom hit and we sat at 9k, then it calmed down to 5.5 to 6k, and we still have that amount of players if not more. Especially more dedicated players that stuck around all this time.

@{5b6b4e8cb1b04a6db0be465d|full_name}: But searching a party to talk to people and have discussions about topics is essentially what having a "chat" is about. Currently Public does not fit the criteria for the "chat" part. Too many cliques, memes and a extremely negative environment where you have to wade through hundreds if not thousands of individuals over and over jumping Pug worlds to find someone able to hold a normal conversation and most of the time these encounters are towards you and not the other way around. 

You're right this isn't a MMO, Group Finders in MMO are anti-social tools, however if you put such a tool in a platform which is solely based around socialization. It would fare a lot better since right now many people feel left out from any meaningful encounters with individiuals solely based on the RNG of Public (And the Rank System..) and people want to conversate. But, they just don't have a tool to conversate about whatever they want right now with other individuals who want to conversate about the same thing.

Hence the group finder solution which would make it easy for anyone to jump into VRChat, create a group with what they want to talk about have people join them and just talk and meet new people who share their same interests or for people to check the group finder list for anything they might be interested in if they don't feel comfortable creating the group and what not. At the end the group simply disbands and vanishes after the group leader logs off or the group leader disbands it via a button in the UI.

Again read my comment again, public is extremely frustrating right now and the staff won't consider moderation changes to it. Group Finder would give them a easy solution so that people who dislike the randomness and wild west environment can side step it altogether and they won't have to do anything personnel wise to "fix" the platform.

@{5c19159361fb5428aa891746|full_name}: I agree with this. My solution is definitely not the be all fix all. Really it is pointing out a simple issue and then the over arching issue it can cause down the road and to some degree has caused now. We can only take steps such as this to prevent the over arching issue from happening.

details:
Community cohesion is extremely important when it comes down to social games. One would argue that it is the second most important thing only being topped by security. If your game has a broken social system then the community cohesion won't last long.

Right now in VRC if "A" person sends an invite to "B" person and they don't know why their invite is never answered it will create doubt thus undermining community cohesion. Rinse and repeat this a few times and suddenly you have a recipe for a jaded player who feels left out. 

You have no idea what the friend is doing with the invite once they receive it. In some instances somebody can be blue status but be in a world that doesn't allow them to accept invites. This creates a situation where the game asks if you would like to notify the host of the room to invite them but we know that feature doesn't work. On top of that if you were to send a normal invite and it is declined it would make life easier knowing it was manually declined.

There is no reason a player should sit in a world and wonder where their invite is going for an hour. Having to take off their headset and DM a player hoping they notice the DM and await a response. Nothing has undermined community cohesion more than this exact moment.

That is the moment of doubt. It is the moment where you wonder if the people you hang out with has found new friends and has forgotten you. You fear the worst as people do and try to come to terms with this. This doubt in this moment can be fixed with a bit of transparency.

In the next update I hope to see this fixed. The system needs a complete overhaul to become more community driven and better to use. It isn't as simple as snapping your fingers and instantly having a better system I understand this. But regardless of work load this needs fixed for the community's sake.

If it isn't fixed there won't be much of a community left in the next year. On steam trends the game has been on a steady decline of actives users after January. Going from 9000 concurrent to over 5k. Hopefully we see a shift in growth soon brought about by better social features. Thank you for your time.
title: Invite and Request System Must be Overhauled to Prevent Further Loss in Community Cohesion
